plan.title: KO x drug interaction DE in brain RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question — does the drug act differently in KO than in WT — is literally a genotype x treatment interaction test on a balanced 2x2 factorial bulk RNA-seq design (16 samples, 4 per cell; counts.csv is 12000 genes x 17 columns, i.e. a gene-symbol column plus 16 sample columns; metadata.csv has 16 rows with genotype (WT/KO), treatment (vehicle/drug) and a combined condition label). The plan therefore centres on one primary inferential step: a negative-binomial GLM with the ~ genotype + treatment + genotype:treatment design, with the interaction coefficient as the answer. Everything else exists to make that test interpretable or to guard against it being read too generously.

T1S1 builds the analysis-ready object: joins counts to metadata by sample ID, verifies the 4/4/4/4 cell balance, filters low-count genes, applies VST/rlog, and runs PCA plus sample-sample correlation to check that the four groups separate and that no sample is an outlier. With n=4 per cell a single bad sample materially changes the interaction estimate, so this QC is not decorative. T1S2 runs the full factorial model and extracts, from the same fit, the interaction contrast plus the two simple effects (drug-vs-vehicle within WT, drug-vs-vehicle within KO) and the main effects — all with independent shrinkage-free effect sizes reported alongside shrunk LFCs where a shrinkage estimator is importable. T1S3 is the honesty step: it classifies genes into the standard interaction quadrants (drug-responsive in WT only, KO only, both same direction, opposite direction / reversed) using both the interaction FDR and the simple-effect statistics, and explicitly reports the count of genes whose 'KO-specific' label rests only on a threshold crossing in one genotype and not on a significant interaction — the single most common overstatement in 2x2 designs. It also reports the achieved power context: 4 replicates per cell gives an interaction test roughly half as powerful as a main effect, so an empty interaction list is a plausible true result and must be reported as such rather than backfilled with simple effects.

T2S1 takes the interaction-ranked gene list into functional interpretation. No reference store is provisioned at planning time, so this step must resolve gene sets against whatever the environment actually holds at run time and, if nothing is available, fall back to an over-representation test against gene sets carried by an installed annotation package; if neither exists it reports the gap and the run still delivers its primary answer from T1S2/T1S3. The package inventory could not be read either, so every step is instructed to probe its imports first and to fall back along a named chain (DESeq2 -> edgeR glmQLF -> limma-voom; pydeseq2 on the Python side) rather than assume any one library.

What this plan will not do: it will not claim a drug mechanism from an interaction gene list, and it will not treat 'significant in KO, not significant in WT' as evidence of differential drug action.
